name.en: Fake Revenue message: a tax refund, an urgent payment or an audit

how.en: An email, text or call that claims to be from Revenue says you are due a tax refund, must make an urgent payment, or are due an audit. It includes a link and asks for personal or banking details. Revenue does not correspond with customers through ordinary email or text, and will never ask for financial information during a phone call.

text.en: An email, text or call says it is from Revenue.
It says you are due a refund, or must pay or face an audit.
It gives a link to claim or pay.
It asks for your bank or card details.

Revenue Commissioners – Notice of Overpayment. Following a review of your PAYE record you are entitled to a refund of €348.60. To have the funds lodged to your account, confirm your bank details within 72 hours: [link]

en: text from revenue saying im due a refund
revenue audit email with a link
revenue asked for my bank details
ros myaccount email asking me to log in
A refund or a bill from Revenue by email or text: Revenue doesn’t contact you this way.
A link to claim or pay.
A caller from “Revenue” asking for financial details.
Don’t click. Log in to myAccount or ROS yourself to see what you really owe or are owed.
If you entered your password, change it. If you gave card or bank details, call your bank.
Report it to the Gardaí and delete the message.

sources.title: Revenue provides further warning on fraudulent communications
